definitions: To interpret something in two different or contradictory ways.
To want to have the benefits of two opposing things simultaneously.
examples: You can't take that comment both ways; it's either a compliment or an insult.
She wants the freedom of being single but also the security of a relationship; she's trying to take it both ways.
He tries to take every situation both ways, never committing to a single viewpoint.
synonyms: play both ends against the middle
